title: Aortic Banding in Mice
author: Dale Abel
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.7rvhm66

steps.title: Anesthetize mouse
steps.instruction: Induce anesthesia with 1% isoflurane delivered via a nose cone.

steps.title: Prepare surgical site
steps.instruction: Apply a topical depilatory agent to the neck and chest, then clean the area with betadine followed by alcohol.

steps.title: Position mouse and maintain temperature
steps.instruction: Place the mouse supine on a heating pad set to maintain body temperature at 37 °C.

steps.title: Make skin incision and expose sternum
steps.instruction: Make a horizontal skin incision of approximately 0.5–1.0 cm at the level of the suprasternal notch, retract the thyroid, and create a 2–3 mm longitudinal cut in the proximal sternum to visualize the aortic arch under low‑power magnification.

steps.title: Pass wire and place suture
steps.instruction: Pass a wire with a snare on its end under the aorta between the origin of the right innominate and left common carotid arteries, snare a 6‑0 silk suture with the wire, and pull the suture back around the aorta.

steps.title: Tie aortic band
steps.instruction: Place a bent 27‑gauge needle next to the aortic arch, snugly tie the suture around the needle and the aorta, then quickly remove the needle.

steps.title: Close incision and recover
steps.instruction: Close the skin, then allow the mouse to recover on a warming pad until fully awake.
